The reusable transformation: parse a mixed-spelling usage JSONL and sum prompt/completion tokens for assistant entries. That's exactly check.py's compute logic. Given the five tasks share a recurring kind of work, this parser is a good candidate.

arguments.name: usage-totals
arguments.source:
(lambda (input)
  (let ((prompt 0) (completion 0))
    (flet ((num (obj &rest keys)
             (dolist (k keys 0)
               (let ((v (gethash k obj)))
                 (when (and v (numberp v)) (return v))))))
      (dolist (line (uiop:split-string input :separator '(#\Newline)))
        (when (plusp (length line))
          (let* ((entry (json:decode-json-from-string line))
                 (payload (gethash "payload" entry)))
            (when (and payload (string= (gethash "role" payload) "assistant"))
              (let ((usage (gethash "usage" payload)))
                (when usage
                  (incf prompt (num usage "prompt_tokens" "input_tokens"))
                  (incf completion (num usage "completion_tokens" "output_tokens"))))))))
      (format nil "prompt ~a~%completion ~a~%total ~a" prompt completion (+ prompt completion)))))
arguments.note: Sum prompt/completion tokens from a mixed-spelling usage JSONL, assistant entries only
